notes:
Summary: Enterprise contact center vendor building a post-call intelligence layer for mid/large customers. Focused on automated post-call summaries, QA highlights, coaching snippets, and one-click ticket creation. Short fragments, customer quotes, and meeting outcomes below.

Key customer requirements (from AE/SE calls):
- Need 99th-pct latency < 800ms for summary-first use (agents expect near-real-time post-call card).
- Batch nightly retrain/eval for quality metrics; streaming summary at call-end.
- Must support on-prem transcription ingestion and redaction pipeline; data residency EU + US.
- Function/tool-calling to push summary -> Zendesk ticket and to trigger coaching tasks in Salesforce.
- Fallback routing: degrade to fast extractive summary model when GPU pool is saturated.
- Accuracy threshold: 85% QA agreement with human QA across key categories (compliance, escalation flags).

Direct quotes / call snippets:
- "If summaries miss escalation signal we generate extra work — false negatives are dealbreaker." (Head of QA)
- "We need a canary during peak Friday spikes — 450 agents making calls at once." (Ops lead)

POC ask on first call:
- 2-week POC with 1K calls sampled (mixed EN/ES), integration to their on-prem ASR export, evaluation on recall for escalation flags and length-normalized summary quality.
- Provide latency and token-cost estimates for both hosted and dedicated paths.

Security/legal thread:
- Legal asked for redaction guarantees in Drive doc (see linked_drive_docs).
- They require KMS integration and key custody for private deployment.

Integration notes:
- Will map call metadata to CRM objects: call_id -> Zendesk ticket, rep_id -> Salesforce user.
- Prefer webhook + function-calling pattern to enable idempotent ticket creation.
- Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching/caching) to reduce per-token spend on nightly QA evaluations.

Risks called out by SE:
- ASR variability across accents (LATAM Spanish / NA regional accents) may drive quality gaps.
- Peak concurrency: scheduled daily spikes 16:00-18:30 PST, plus irregular marketing surges. Need autoscale and predictable tail latency.

Immediate AE notes / next tasks:
- Send updated POC SOW by 2024-11-05.
- Arrange infra scoping with infra eng + security (requested 1-hr slot week of 2024-11-08).
- Provide sample cost calc: dedicated pool for 450 concurrent decoders + fallback hosted burst.

Short-hand CRM fragments (copied from call notes):
- 10/12 intro call: interested, legal + infra loop.
- 10/30 deep-dive w/ QA + Ops. Action: sample dataset upload instructions.
- 11/01 demo: showed streaming-endcard + function-calling -> Zendesk. Positive on UX.
- 11/01 ask: show cold-start latency w/ 1s token pacing, suggest quantized model variant for cost.

poc_details: Length: 2 weeks. Scope: ingest 1k anonymized calls from on-prem ASR export -> Redwood POC endpoint; evaluate summary fidelity (ROUGE + human QA), escalation recall, end-to-end latency. Success criteria: escalation recall >= 85%, mean summary quality score >= 4/5 in QA rubric, 99th-pct latency < 1s under 1x concurrency and <1.2s under 2x. Delivery: infra diagram, SOW, cost model, and sample rollout plan.
use_case_summary: Primary: post-call summaries for agent wrap-up and automated ticket creation; secondary: QA sampling and coach highlight extraction. Needs function-calling to CRM, streaming endcard UI, reliable fallback during GPU saturation, and opt-in on-prem ingestion for regulated clients.
sla_targets: 99.9% uptime on Dedicated; 99th percentile summary latency target 800-1200ms depending on model; throughput to support 450 concurrent decode streams with burst to 700 for marketing surge.
scale_requirements: Baseline: 450 concurrent decoding sessions (avg call length 4m). Expected daily calls: 12k. Nightly batch eval up to 50k tokens for QA pipelines.
spike_patterns: Daily peak 16:00-18:30 PST weekdays. Marketing events create irregular spikes (~150% baseline) ~ quarterly. Need autoscale + graceful fallback to lower-cost extractive summaries during sustained overload.
